title: Portable Execution-Graph Learning Records for Fractal CLI and Fractal Voice
summary: Extend the Rust Fractal CLI and native macOS Fractal Voice app so every portable .fractal/project.fractal execution graph carries compact, structurally meaningful, backward-compatible node learning records, graph-edit decisions, and aggregate completion outcomes, while large evidence remains externally referenced.

architecture.approach: Add a versioned, strongly typed learning-data layer to the existing fractal.execution_graph.v1 and fractal.project.v1 documents. Keep graph topology authoritative, mirror dependency IDs into normalized node learning records, and centralize defaulting, controlled-value validation, lifecycle mutation, event recording, external-reference hygiene, and deterministic graph-outcome aggregation in Rust. Existing graph construction, execution, evolution/amendment, persistence, and sync paths call this layer at their current boundaries. The Swift app uses tolerant Codable projections for the same additive fields so older and newer project files both decode and display safely.
architecture.rationale: An additive typed layer preserves current graph hashes, topology, and old-file readability while preventing producers from inventing incompatible values. Central lifecycle and aggregation APIs make timestamps, attempts, verification, costs, artifact lineage, human intervention, and final metrics consistent across local execution, resume, cancellation, graph evolution, and cloud sync. Compact evidence IDs avoid graph bloat and sensitive transcript capture, while deterministic derivation makes the learning data testable rather than speculative.

components.name: Learning Data Contract
components.responsibility: Own controlled enums and serializable node records, graph-edit events, graph outcomes, external evidence/artifact references, backward-compatible defaults, normalization, and validation.
components.technology: Rust, serde, serde_json, RFC 3339 timestamps, SHA-256 graph hashes

components.name: Graph Producers and Lifecycle Recorder
components.responsibility: Initialize structural metadata and update attempts, timing, executor identity, controlled outcomes/failures, verification evidence, artifacts, consumers, intervention, costs, and notes at every runtime transition.
components.technology: Existing Rust modules compile.rs, decompose.rs, project_file.rs, execute.rs, orchestrate.rs, supervise.rs, run_control.rs, and checkpoint.rs

components.name: Graph Edit Decision Journal
components.responsibility: Record compact split, reroute, cancel, and dependency-edit decisions with before-hash, trigger, actor, affected nodes, timestamp, and eventual effect.
components.technology: Existing Rust amendment and governed-evolution paths using append-only typed JSON events

components.name: Outcome Aggregator
components.responsibility: Derive graph-level success, acceptance results, durations, concurrency, cost, retry/reopen/dead-node/intervention counts, verification coverage, and early-stop or unnecessary-expansion flags from recorded facts.
components.technology: Deterministic Rust graph analysis over topology and lifecycle records

components.name: Portable Persistence and Sync Boundary
components.responsibility: Migrate/default old documents on read, validate and atomically persist enriched documents, preserve unknown compatible data, reject oversized or forbidden embedded content, and upload the exact validated portable representation.
components.technology: Rust serde, atomic file writes, existing graph_store and project_sync modules

components.name: Fractal Voice Graph Projection
components.responsibility: Tolerantly decode and present enriched project graph status without requiring new fields in legacy files.
components.technology: Swift Codable, SwiftUI, XCTest via Swift Package Manager

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A newly compiled graph gives every node a stable ID and type, objective, normalized dependency IDs, created/ready/start/finish timestamps as applicable, executor identity fields, attempt count, controlled outcome and failure code, verification record, produced and consumed artifact references, human-intervention record, estimated and actual cost, and optional bounded notes.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run focused Rust producer and lifecycle tests with cargo test compile project_file execute orchestrate supervise; fixtures must assert exact serialized fields and timestamp/attempt transitions.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Only the seven requested outcomes and twelve requested failure codes are accepted; incompatible state combinations such as verified_success with failed verification, a failure code on verified_success, finished outcomes without finished_at, or consumed artifact IDs that were never produced are rejected.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run Rust contract table tests that deserialize every allowed value and reject unknown values and invalid cross-field combinations via cargo test learning_data.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Existing fractal.project.v1 files and fractal.execution_graph.v1 graphs that omit all learning fields still load, receive deterministic safe defaults or nulls, persist, reload, and retain their original graph topology and identity without data loss.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run legacy-fixture migration and JSON serialization round-trip tests in project_file and graph_store with cargo test project_file graph_store.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Checkout, retry, execution failure, verification failure, success, cancellation, stale-release/resume, artifact production and consumption, and human completion each update attempts, timestamps, executor metadata, controlled outcome/failure, verification evidence, intervention, and costs consistently and atomically.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run lifecycle scenario tests covering every named transition with cargo test execute project_file run_control checkpoint and assert monotonic timestamps, attempt increments, preserved prior facts, and controlled terminal states.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Human split, reroute, cancel, and dependency edits, plus autonomous graph evolution, append compact decision events containing graph_before_hash, controlled action with target and created_nodes, trigger, actor, timestamp, and eventual_effect fields success and rework_reduced.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run amendment/evolution event tests with cargo test amendments harness_evolution supervise; verify before-hash correctness, action payloads, event ordering, and later eventual-effect updates.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: When a graph reaches a terminal project state, it records final_verified_success, per-acceptance passed/failed status, total and critical-path duration, total agent time, maximum parallelism, total cost, retries, reopened nodes, dead or unused nodes, human intervention count, verification coverage, stopped-too-early, and expanded-unnecessarily from recorded facts.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run deterministic aggregation tests over sequential, parallel, retried, reopened, dead-node, failed-verification, cancelled, and human-completed fixtures with cargo test learning_data project_file.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Graph files contain only compact IDs and bounded notes for evidence, logs, and artifacts; chain-of-thought, generated-token streams, huge terminal transcripts, speculative metrics, arbitrary self-ratings, secrets, and oversized inline payloads are rejected or omitted.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run validator boundary tests with forbidden keys and oversized strings/arrays using cargo test project_file graph_store, and inspect representative serialized fixtures to confirm only evidence_refs and artifact IDs are stored.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Local persistence, evolved-child persistence, resume/checkpoint recovery, graph validation/hash verification, and Fractal Society sync all preserve and transmit the same enriched learning records without silently dropping fields.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run persistence/evolution/sync fixture tests with cargo test project_file graph_store project_sync checkpoint harness_evolution and compare canonical pre/post boundary JSON.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Fractal Voice decodes both legacy and enriched project.fractal fixtures and displays the available node outcome, attempt, verification, and graph completion summary without crashing or treating missing additive fields as corruption.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run swift test --package-path macos/FractalVoice and assert XCTest coverage for legacy, fully enriched, partially populated, and unknown-forward-compatible fixtures.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The repository passes formatting, the complete Rust test suite, warning-free Clippy, and the native Swift test suite, with no generated dist release bundle changed and no signing, notarization, packaging, or Apple submission invoked.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo test --no-fail-fast; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; swift test --package-path macos/FractalVoice; then verify git diff --name-only contains no path beginning with dist- or generated release bundle.

non_goals: Apple code signing, notarization, App Store submission, release upload, DMG/ZIP generation, or modification of any generated dist release bundle.
Embedding large logs, artifact bodies, terminal transcripts, prompts, chain-of-thought, token-by-token model output, or binary evidence in project.fractal.
Adding speculative quality scores, arbitrary model self-evaluations, or metrics that cannot be derived from recorded lifecycle and topology facts.
Replacing the existing execution graph schema, scheduler, graph hash, project identity, Fractal Society protocol, or external artifact/log storage systems.
Building a training pipeline or changing model-selection policy; this work only records compact trustworthy learning data.
Reconstructing precise historical timing, executor, verification, or cost facts that are absent from legacy graphs.
